opening.argument: The video reports on a past Wells Fargo settlement and fake-accounts scandal. It attributes millions of fraudulent accounts to employees under pressure to meet sales goals, and describes forged signatures, unauthorized debit-card activation, and transfers to unauthorized accounts as conduct being reported, not actions viewers are asked to take. The closing screen asks viewers to watch more or subscribe, but that ordinary channel invitation is not tied to payment, investment, credentials, or any other financial action. The scandal is the subject of the news coverage; the video does not make a financial offer to its audience.

citations.quote: Wells Fargo To Pay $3 Billion In Settlement For Fake Accounts Scandal
After employees under pressure to meet sales goals created millions of fraudulent bank accounts between 2002 and 2016.
Forging customer signatures, creating pins to activate unauthorized debit cards,. And moving money to unauthorized accounts.
